answer: Work fingerprint binding ties each identity to a distinctive runtime signature, such as timing jitter or a cipher handshake trace, and admits new identities only when their signature diverges from all active ones. Each admitted identity must also post a small escrow in timber-denominated credits that is forfeited if its signature later clusters with another. Clones therefore pay registration, escrow, and detection risk while their marginal revenue stays capped by genuine demand. The escrow floor, calibrated in basalt-weighted units, makes every extra clone strictly negative-EV.
